Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Paralegal (Clinical Negligence) position at your Reading firm. My background in disputes, case management and client-facing legal work maps directly onto the responsibilities you have described, and I am keen to bring that experience to a clinical negligence caseload.

At Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner, I supported both international arbitration and real estate disputes across the full lifecycle of proceedings: reviewing and organising evidence, preparing hearing bundles, drafting procedural documents, tracking deadlines and coordinating with clients on outstanding matters. Shortly before a significant submission deadline I became the only junior supporting the arbitration team, taking responsibility for document coordination and ensuring on-time delivery — feedback from the partner and associate placed my performance at newly qualified solicitor level.

In my current role at Citizens Advice East Berkshire I manage matters independently from initial instruction through to submission. I interview clients on sensitive matters, take detailed factual statements, identify evidential gaps and draft correspondence and procedural applications — all while translating complex rules into clear, practical guidance for people in difficult circumstances. That combination of rigorous case preparation and considered client communication is, I understand, central to clinical negligence work, where clients are often vulnerable and the procedural stakes are high.

I am familiar with the discipline required to manage competing deadlines across a live caseload, maintain accurate and confidential case records, and draft documents to a standard that can go directly to partners and counsel. I am also comfortable working in an environment where attention to detail and sound judgement on priorities are non-negotiable.

Reading is my local area and I am available to start promptly. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your team.

Yours faithfully,
Maria Fernanda Silva
